# Civ VI Full-Anthology Reference — Vol 2: Civilizations & Leaders N–Z

<!-- generated by Stage 2 reference build, 2026-08-03 -->
> **Game configuration this volume describes:** RULESET_EXPANSION_2 (Gathering
> Storm ruleset, which includes all Rise & Fall content) + every official DLC
> pack. Optional game modes (Heroes, Secret Societies, Monopolies, Barbarian
> Clans, Apocalypse, Zombies, etc.) are **not** included — the live capture
> calibration shows they are off in this game. Scenario-only content excluded.
>
> **Sourcing:** every value is machine-extracted from the game's own data files
> (base + Expansion1 + Expansion2 XML and each DLC pack's Data XML, merged in
> the game's modinfo-declared load order). Nothing comes from model memory.
> Verified against the live game DB: 36 districts (26 specialty), 54 resources
> (34 luxuries), 7 victories, 8 governors / 48 promotions — all exact matches.
>
> **Trust order if something disagrees:** 1) the live snapshot from the
> tracker, 2) this document, 3) anything else. Mods (e.g. Real Strategy) can
> shift values; the live snapshot always wins.

**17 civilizations (N–Z), 21 leader entries.** Leader personas (e.g. the Rulers packs) are separate leader entries under their civilization.

## Netherlands
- **Civ ability — Grote Rivieren:** Major adjacency bonus for Campuses, Theater Squares, and Industrial Zones if next to a river. Culture Bomb adjacent tiles when completing a Harbor. +50% Production toward the Dam district and Flood Barrier building.
- **Unique Unit — De Zeven Provinciën:** [CS 50, RS 60 (range 2), moves 4, cost 280, maint 5] Netherlands unique Renaissance Era unit that replaces the Frigate. +7 Combat Strength when attacking defensible districts.
- **Unique Improvement — Polder:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct a Polder, unique to Netherlands. +1 Food, +1 Production, and +0.5 Housing. +1 Food if adjacent to a Polder improvement. Additional Production, Gold, and Food as you advance through the Civics and Technology Tree. Must be placed on a Coast or Lake tile adjacent to 3 or more passable land tiles. Increases Movement Cost of tile to 3.
- **Start bias:** Coast and Lake (tier 4); Rivers (tier 2)

### Leader: Wilhelmina
- **Ability — Radio Oranje:** Your Trade Routes to your own cities provide +2 Loyalty per turn for the starting city. Trade Routes to foreign cities or from foreign cities provide +2 Culture to you.
- **Agenda — Billionaire:** Tries to maximize Trade Routes. Likes civilizations that trade with her, dislikes those who do not.

## Norway
- **Civ ability — Knarr:** Units gain the ability to enter Ocean tiles after researching the Shipbuilding technology. Naval melee units heal in neutral territory. Units ignore additional Movement costs from embarking and disembarking.
- **Unique Unit — Berserker:** [CS 48, moves 2, cost 160, maint 3] Norwegian unique Medieval era melee unit that replaces the Man-At-Arms. 4 Movement if this unit starts in enemy territory. +10 Combat Strength when attacking and -5 Combat Strength when defending against melee attacks.
- **Unique Building — Stave Church:** [cost 120, maint 2] A building unique to Norway. Required to purchase Apostles and Inquisitors with Faith. Holy Site districts get an additional standard adjacency bonus from Woods. +1 Production to each coastal resource tile in this city.
- **Start bias:** Coast and Lake (tier 3); Woods (tier 5)

### Leader: Harald Hardrada (Varangian)
- **Ability — Varangian Guard:** All units pay 2 less Gold maintenance. 75% Discount on Levying units and levied units receive Culture, Faith and Science from kills equal to 50% of the opponents' Combat Strength. +1 Influence Points per turn from the Stave Church.
- **Agenda — Harald's Saga:** Emphasizes protectorate wars. Admires civilizations that start protectorate wars. Dislikes civilizations that attack city states.

### Leader: Harald Hardrada
- **Ability — Thunderbolt of the North:** Allows coastal raiding for all naval melee units and +50% Production toward all naval melee units. Receive Science from pillaging and coastal raiding Mines in addition to Gold. Pillaging or coastal raiding Quarries, Pastures, Plantations, and Camps provide Culture in addition to Faith. Gain the Viking Longship unique unit with Sailing.
- **Agenda — Last Viking King:** Builds a large navy and respects civilizations who follow their lead. Does not like civilizations with a weak navy.

## Nubia
- **Civ ability — Ta-Seti:** +30% Production toward Ranged units. All Ranged units gain +50% combat experience. Mines over strategic resources provide +1 Production. Mines over bonus and luxury resources provide +2 Gold.
- **Unique Unit — Pítati Archer:** [CS 17, RS 30 (range 2), moves 3, cost 70, maint 1] Nubian unique Ancient era unit that replaces the Archer. Stronger than the Archer with extra Movement. Upgrades to Crossbowman.
- **Unique Improvement — Nubian Pyramid:** Improvement that unlocks with Masonry and must be built on Desert, Desert Hills or Floodplains. +2 Faith and +2 Food. Receives additional yields from adjacent districts. +1 Food if adjacent to a city center. For all other districts that award adjacency bonuses: +1 of the appropriate yield if that district is adjacent.
- **Start bias:** Desert (tier 1); Desert (Hills) (tier 1); Copper (tier 5); Diamonds (tier 5); Jade (tier 5); Mercury (tier 5); Salt (tier 5); Silver (tier 5); Aluminum (tier 5); Coal (tier 5); Iron (tier 5); Niter (tier 5); Uranium (tier 5)

### Leader: Amanitore
- **Ability — Kandake of Meroë:** +20% Production towards all districts rising to +40% if there is a Nubian Pyramid adjacent to the City Center.
- **Agenda — City Planner:** Always tries to keep the maximum number of districts in each city. Respects other civilizations who also develop their cities in this fashion.

## Ottomans
- **Civ ability — Great Turkish Bombard:** +50% Production toward siege units. All siege units gain +5 Combat Strength against district defenses. Conquered cities do not lose Population. Cities not founded by the Ottomans gain +1 Amenity and +4 Loyalty per turn.
- **Unique Unit — Barbary Corsair:** [CS 40, RS 50 (range 2), moves 4, cost 240, maint 3] Ottoman unique Medieval era naval unit that replaces the Privateer. It costs no Movement to coastal raid. Can only be seen by other Naval Raiders unless adjacent to it. Reveals Naval Raiders within sight range.
- **Unique Building — Grand Bazaar:** [cost 220, maint 0] A building unique to the Ottomans. Accumulate 1 extra Strategic resource for every different type of Strategic resource this city has improved. Receive 1 Amenity for every Luxury resource this city has improved.
- **Start bias:** Niter (tier 5)

### Leader: Suleiman
- **Ability — Grand Vizier:** Exclusive unique Governor with military and diplomatic abilities. Gain the Janissary unique unit and a Governor Title when the Gunpowder technology is researched.
- **Agenda — Lawgiver:** Keeps his citizens happy and loyal. Impressed by those with similar priorities, especially if their cities were founded by many players. Dislikes those with happiness/loyalty issues or few captured cities.

### Leader: Suleiman (Muhteşem)
- **Ability — The Magnificent:** +15% Science and Culture when in a Golden Age or Heroic Age. +4 Combat Strength when not in a Golden Age or Heroic Age against Civilizations who are also not in a Golden Age or Heroic Age.
- **Agenda — Golden Age of Suleiman:** Impressed by any civilization that earns a Golden Age. Dislikes those in Dark Ages.

## Persia
- **Civ ability — Satrapies:** +1 Trade Route capacity with Political Philosophy civic. Receive +2 Gold and +1 Culture for routes between your own cities. Roads built in your territory are one level more advanced than usual.
- **Unique Unit — Immortal:** [CS 35, RS 25 (range 2), moves 2, cost 100, maint 2] Persian unique melee unit that replaces the Swordsman. Melee class unit with a ranged attack, Range 2. Strong defense strength.
- **Unique Improvement — Pairidaeza:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct a Pairidaeza, unique to Persia. +1 Culture and +2 Gold. +1 Appeal. +1 Culture for each adjacent Holy Site and Theater Square. +1 Gold for each adjacent Commercial Hub and City Center. Additional Culture and Tourism as you advance through the Technology and Civics Tree. Cannot be built on Snow, Tundra, Snow Hills, or Tundra Hills or adjacent to another Pairidaeza.

### Leader: Cyrus
- **Ability — Fall of Babylon:** +2 Movement for the first 10 turns after declaring a Surprise War on a major civilization. +5 Loyalty per turn in occupied cities with a garrisoned unit. Declaring a Surprise War only counts as a Formal War for the purposes of Grievances and warmongering.
- **Agenda — Opportunist:** Likes leaders who have declared a Surprise War. Dismisses leaders who do not use Surprise War declarations.

### Leader: Nader Shah
- **Ability — Sword of Persia:** +5 Combat Strength when attacking full Health Units. Cities not founded by Nader Shah receive +2 Faith and +3 Gold on Domestic Trade Routes.
- **Agenda — Jazayerchi:** Likes civilizations with a high amount of land units. Dislikes civilizations with a low amount of land units.

## Phoenicia
- **Civ ability — Mediterranean Colonies:** Begin the game with the Writing technology Eureka. Coastal cities founded by Phoenicia and located on the same continent as the Phoenician Capital are 100% Loyal. Settlers gain +2 Movement and +2 sight range while embarked. Settlers ignore additional Movement costs from embarking and disembarking.
- **Unique Unit — Bireme:** [CS 35, moves 4, cost 65, maint 1] Phoenician unique Ancient Era unit that replaces the Galley. Increased Combat Strength and Movement. Trader units are immune to being plundered if they are within 4 tiles of a Bireme and on a water tile.
- **Unique District — Cothon:** [cost 27, maint 0] A district unique to Phoenicia for naval activity in your city. Replaces the Harbor district and cheaper to build. Must be built on Coast or Lake Terrain adjacent to land. +50% Production towards naval units and Settlers in this city. All wounded naval units in this city’s borders heal +100 HP each turn.
- **Start bias:** Coast and Lake (tier 2)

### Leader: Dido
- **Ability — Founder of Carthage:** Can move their original Capital to any city with a Cothon they founded by completing a unique project in that city. +1 Trade Route capacity for each Government Plaza building and the Government Plaza district. +50% Production toward districts in the city with the Government Plaza.
- **Agenda — Sicilian Wars:** Wants to settle coastal cities. Likes those who settle inland. Dislikes those with mostly coastal cities.

## Poland
- **Civ ability — Golden Liberty:** Culture Bomb adjacent tiles when completing an Encampment or Fort inside friendly territory. One Military policy slot in the current government is converted to a Wildcard slot.
- **Unique Unit — Winged Hussar:** [CS 64, moves 4, cost 330, maint 5] Polish unique Renaissance era unit. Pushes defending enemy units back from their hex in any battle where they score more damage. Defenders that cannot retreat suffer additional damage.
- **Unique Building — Sukiennice:** [cost 120, maint 0] A building unique to Poland. International Trade Routes from this city gain +2 Production; domestic Trade Routes gain +4 Gold.

### Leader: Jadwiga
- **Ability — Lithuanian Union:** Poland's majority religion becomes the dominant religion in cities that loses a tile to a Polish Culture Bomb. Holy Sites gain a Faith adjacency bonus from adjacent Districts. All Relics provide bonus Faith (+2), Culture (+2) and Gold (+4).
- **Agenda — Saint:** Tries to build up Faith, and likes civilizations that also focus on Faith.

## Portugal
- **Civ ability — Casa da Índia:** International Trade Routes must originate from a coastal city and can only reach cities on the coast or with a Harbor, but receive +50% towards all yields. Trader units have +50% range over water, and can embark as soon as they are unlocked.
- **Unique Unit — Nau:** [CS 55, moves 4, cost 240, maint 2] Portuguese unique naval melee unit that replaces the Caravel. Starts with 1 free Promotion and is less maintenance. Has two charges to build Feitorias.
- **Unique Building — Navigation School:** [cost 250, maint 2] A building unique to Portugal. +25% Production towards naval units in this city. +1 Science for every two coast or lake tiles in this city. +1 Great Admiral and +1 Great Scientist point per turn.
- **Unique Improvement — Feitoria:** Unlocks the Nau ability to construct a Feitoria, unique to Portugal. Provides +4 Gold and +1 Production. Trade routes sent to this city from Portugal gain +4 Gold and +1 Production. Can only be built adjacent to Luxury or Bonus resources in territory belonging to other Civilizations or City-States that you have Open Borders with. Must be built on a Coast or Lake tile adjacent to land and not adjacent to another Feitoria. Feitorias cannot be removed.
- **Start bias:** Coast and Lake (tier 1)

### Leader: João III
- **Ability — Porta do Cerco:** All units receive +1 sight. +1 Trade Route capacity when a civilization is met. Open Borders with all city-states.
- **Agenda — Navigator's Legacy:** Appreciates civilizations who explore the world, and dislikes those who stay close to their borders.

## Rome
- **Civ ability — All Roads Lead to Rome:** All cities you found or conquer start with a Trading Post. If in Trade Route range of your Capital, they also start with a road to it. Your Trade Routes earn +1 Gold for passing through Trading Posts in your own cities.
- **Unique Unit — Legion:** [CS 40, moves 2, cost 110, maint 2] Roman unique Classical era melee unit that replaces the Swordsman. Can build a Roman Fort.
- **Unique District — Bath:** [cost 18, maint 0] A district unique to Rome for city growth. Replaces the Aqueduct district and cheaper to build. It provides this city with a source of fresh water from an adjacent River, Lake, Oasis, or Mountain. Cities that do not yet have existing fresh water receive up to 6 Housing. Cities that already have existing fresh water will instead get +2 Housing. If built adjacent to a Geothermal Fissure +1 Amenity. In all cases the Bath provides an additional bonus of +2 Housing and +1 Amenity. Prevents Food loss during Drought. Must be built adjacent to the City Center. Military Engineers can spend a charge to complete 20% of a Bath's production.

### Leader: Julius Caesar
- **Ability — Veni, Vidi, Vici:** +300 Gold whenever you conquer a city for the first time or when you earn Gold from a Barbarian Outpost. The Gold becomes 500 after researching Metal Casting and 700 after Steel (on Standard Speed). When targeting Barbarians receive +5 Combat Strength and always earn normal XP.
- **Agenda — Gallic Wars:** Hates barbarians. Likes civilizations that clear out barbarian outposts. Does not like civilizations that ignore barbarian outposts.

### Leader: Trajan
- **Ability — Trajan's Column:** All cities start with an additional City Center building. (Starts with a Monument building in the Ancient era).
- **Agenda — Optimus Princeps:** Tries to include as much territory as possible in their empire. Does not like civilizations who control little territory.

## Russia
- **Civ ability — Mother Russia:** Extra territory upon founding cities. +1 Faith and +1 Production from Tundra. Units do not receive damage from Blizzards. Civilizations that are at war with Russia receive +100% unit damage from Blizzards in Russian territory.
- **Unique Unit — Cossack:** [CS 67, moves 5, cost 340, maint 5] Russian unique Industrial era unit that replaces Cavalry. Stronger than Cavalry, and gains +5 Combat Strength when fighting in or adjacent to its home territory. Can move after attacking if Movement points remain.
- **Unique District — Lavra:** [cost 27, maint 1] A district unique to Russia for religious activity. Replaces the Holy Site district and cheaper to build. Your city border grows by one tile each time a Great Person is expended in this city. The Lavra provides +1 Great Writer point per turn with a Shrine, +1 Great Artist point per turn with a Temple, and +1 Great Musician point per turn with a Worship building.
- **Start bias:** Tundra (tier 2); Tundra (Hills) (tier 2)

### Leader: Peter
- **Ability — The Grand Embassy:** Receives Science or Culture from Trade Routes to civilizations that are more advanced than Russia. +1 per 3 technologies or civics ahead.
- **Agenda — Westernizer:** Friendly to those civilizations that are ahead of him in Science and Culture. Dislikes backwards civilizations that are lacking in Science and Culture.

## Scotland
- **Civ ability — Scottish Enlightenment:** Happy cities receive an additional +5% Science and +5% Production. Happy cities generate +1 Great Scientist point per Campus and +1 Great Engineer point per Industrial Zone. Ecstatic cities double all these amounts.
- **Unique Unit — Highlander:** [CS 50, RS 65 (range 1), moves 3, cost 380, maint 5] Scottish unique Industrial Era unit that replaces the Ranger. Strong reconnaissance unit. +5 Combat Strength bonus when fighting in Hill and Forest terrain.
- **Unique Improvement — Golf Course:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct a Golf Course, unique to Scotland. +1 Amenity and +2 Gold. +1 Culture if adjacent to a City Center district and +1 Culture if adjacent to an Entertainment Complex district. Additional Tourism and Housing as you advance through the Civics and Technology Tree. Cannot be placed on Desert or Desert Hills. One per city. Tiles with Golf Courses cannot be swapped. +1 Appeal.

### Leader: Robert the Bruce
- **Ability — Bannockburn:** Can declare a War of Liberation after gaining the Defensive Tactics Civic. +100% Production and +2 Movement for the first 10 turns after declaring a War of Liberation.
- **Agenda — Flower of Scotland:** Will not attack neighbors unless they break a promise to him. Likes those who do not war with neighbors, dislikes those who do.

## Scythia
- **Civ ability — People of the Steppe:** Receive a second light cavalry unit or Saka Horse Archer each time you train a light cavalry unit or Saka Horse Archer.
- **Unique Unit — Saka Horse Archer:** [CS 20, RS 25 (range 1), moves 4, cost 100, maint 2] Scythian unique Classical era unit. Ranged unit with 4 Movement with a Range of 1.
- **Unique Improvement — Kurgan:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct a Kurgan, unique to Scythia. +1 Faith and +3 Gold. +1 Faith for each adjacent Pasture (becomes +2 after researching Stirrups). Provides Tourism from Faith after researching Flight. Cannot be built on Hills.
- **Start bias:** Grassland (tier 5); Plains (tier 5); Horses (tier 2)

### Leader: Tomyris
- **Ability — Killer of Cyrus:** All units receive +5 Combat Strength when attacking wounded units. When they eliminate a unit, they heal up to 30 hit points.
- **Agenda — Backstab Averse:** Likes civilizations who are their declared friend. Hates civilizations who backstab and declare surprise wars.

## Spain
- **Civ ability — Treasure Fleet:** May form Fleets and Armadas with Mercantilism, instead of Nationalism and Mobilization. Trade Routes receive +3 Gold, +2 Faith, and +1 Production. Trade Routes between multiple continents receive triple these numbers. Cities not on your original Capital’s continent receive +25% Production towards districts and a builder when founded.
- **Unique Unit — Conquistador:** [CS 58, moves 2, cost 250, maint 4] Spanish unique Renaissance era unit that replaces the Musketman. +10 Combat Strength when there is a religious unit within one hex. If this unit captures a city or is adjacent to a city when it is captured, the city will automatically adopt the Conquistador player's Religion as the dominant Religion.
- **Unique Improvement — Mission:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct a Mission, unique to Spain. +2 Faith. Additional +2 Science once Cultural Heritage is discovered. +2 Faith, +1 Production, and +1 Food if on a different continent than your Capital. +1 Science for every adjacent Campus and Holy Site district.
- **Start bias:** Geothermal Fissure (tier 3)

### Leader: Philip II
- **Ability — El Escorial:** Inquisitors can Remove Heresy one extra time. Inquisitors eliminate 100% of the presence of other Religions. Combat and Religious units have a bonus of +5 Combat Strength against players following other Religions.
- **Agenda — Counter Reformer:** Likes civilizations who follow the same Religion, and wants their cities to all follow the same Religion. Hates anyone trying to spread their Religion into their empire.

## Sumeria
- **Civ ability — Epic Quests:** When you disperse a Barbarian Outpost, receive a Tribal Village reward in addition to the usual Gold. Pay half the usual cost to levy city-state units.
- **Unique Unit — War-Cart:** [CS 30, moves 3, cost 55] Sumerian unique Ancient era unit. Stronger than all other starting units. No penalties against anti-cavalry units. 4 Movement if this unit starts in open terrain.
- **Unique Improvement — Ziggurat:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct a Ziggurat, unique to Sumeria. +2 Science. +1 Culture if next to River. Cannot be built on Hills but may be built on Floodplains.
- **Start bias:** Rivers (tier 3)

### Leader: Gilgamesh
- **Ability — Adventures of Enkidu:** When at war with a common foe, they and their allies share pillage rewards and share combat experience gains if within 5 tiles. Their Alliances gain Alliance Points for being at war with a common foe. +5 Combat Strength against units of players at war with you and your ally.
- **Agenda — Ally of Enkidu:** Likes civilizations who are willing to form a long-term alliance. Dislikes anyone denouncing or attacking his friends and allies.

## Sweden
- **Civ ability — Nobel Prize:** Sweden gains 50 Diplomatic Favor when earning a Great Person (on Standard Speed). Sweden receives +1 Great Engineer point from Factories and +1 Great Scientist point from Universities. Having Sweden in the game adds three unique World Congress competitions starting in the Industrial Era.
- **Unique Unit — Carolean:** [CS 55, moves 3, cost 250, maint 3] Swedish unique Renaissance Era unit that replaces the Pike and Shot. Faster than the Pike and Shot. +3 Combat Strength per unused Movement.
- **Unique Improvement — Open-Air Museum:** Unlocks the Builder ability to construct an Open-Air Museum, unique to Sweden. Provides +2 Loyalty per turn in this city. +2 Culture and +2 Tourism for each type of terrain (Snow, Tundra, Desert, Plains or Grassland) in which at least one Swedish city is founded. One per city. Tiles with Open-Air Museums cannot be swapped.

### Leader: Kristina
- **Ability — Minerva of the North:** Buildings with at least three Great Work slots and wonders with at least two Great Work slots are automatically themed when they have all their slots filled. She may construct the Queen's Bibliotheque in the Government Plaza.
- **Agenda — Bibliophile:** Wants to have more Great Works than anyone else. Likes those who leave the Great Works to her, dislikes those who also have many Great Works.

## Vietnam
- **Civ ability — Nine Dragon River Delta:** All land specialty districts can only be built on Rainforest, Marsh, or Woods. Receive the following yields for every building on these features: +1 Culture in Woods, +1 Science in Rainforest and +1 Production in Marsh. Woods can be planted with the Medieval Faires civic.
- **Unique Unit — Voi Chiến:** [CS 35, RS 40 (range 2), moves 3, cost 200, maint 3] Vietnamese unique Medieval era ranged unit that replaces the Crossbowman. These units have additional movement and can move after attacking. They are also stronger when defending, more expensive, and have greater sight.
- **Unique District — Thành:** [cost 27, maint 1] A district unique to Vietnam which replaces the Encampment. +2 Culture for each adjacent district. After Flight is researched receive Tourism equal to the Culture output. This district does not require population, is cheaper to build, cannot be built adjacent to the city center, does not provide Great People points, and is not a specialty district.
- **Start bias:** Rainforest (tier 1); Woods (tier 1); Marsh (tier 1)

### Leader: Bà Triệu
- **Ability — Drive Out The Aggressors:** +5 Combat Strength for units fighting in Rainforest, Marsh, or Woods tiles. +1 Movement if they begin their turn there. Both these bonuses are doubled if the tile is your territory.
- **Agenda — Defender of the Homeland:** Likes Civilizations who have not declared war on her. Dislikes Civilizations that have declared war on her. For these, her opinion decreases further each turn the war progresses, and this decreased opinion never decays.

## Zulu
- **Civ ability — Isibongo:** Cities with a garrisoned unit get +3 Loyalty per turn, or +5 if it is a Corps or Army. Conquering a city with a unit will upgrade it into a Corps or Army, if the proper Civics are unlocked.
- **Unique Unit — Impi:** [CS 45, moves 2, cost 125, maint 1] Zulu unique Medieval Era unit that replaces the Pikeman. Increased Flanking bonus, low cost and low maintenance. Earns XP faster.
- **Unique District — Ikanda:** [cost 27, maint 1] A district unique to Zulu which replaces the Encampment. Provides +1 Housing. Once the Civic or Technology prerequisite is met, Corps and Armies can be built outright. Buildings in the Ikanda receive +2 Gold and +1 Science. Faster Corps and Army creation.

### Leader: Shaka
- **Ability — Amabutho:** May form Corps (Mercenaries Civic) and Armies (Nationalism Civic) earlier. An additional +5 Base Combat Strength to both Corps and Armies.
- **Agenda — Horn, Chest, Loins:** Tries to use as many corps and armies as possible and respects civilizations who follow his lead. Does not like civilizations who can't create corps or don't use them.

# Civ VI Full-Anthology Reference — Vol 3: Districts, Buildings & Wonders

<!-- generated by Stage 2 reference build, 2026-08-03 -->
> **Game configuration this volume describes:** RULESET_EXPANSION_2 (Gathering
> Storm ruleset, which includes all Rise & Fall content) + every official DLC
> pack. Optional game modes (Heroes, Secret Societies, Monopolies, Barbarian
> Clans, Apocalypse, Zombies, etc.) are **not** included — the live capture
> calibration shows they are off in this game. Scenario-only content excluded.
>
> **Sourcing:** every value is machine-extracted from the game's own data files
> (base + Expansion1 + Expansion2 XML and each DLC pack's Data XML, merged in
> the game's modinfo-declared load order). Nothing comes from model memory.
> Verified against the live game DB: 36 districts (26 specialty), 54 resources
> (34 luxuries), 7 victories, 8 governors / 48 promotions — all exact matches.
>
> **Trust order if something disagrees:** 1) the live snapshot from the
> tracker, 2) this document, 3) anything else. Mods (e.g. Real Strategy) can
> shift values; the live snapshot always wins.

## Districts — all 36 (26 specialty)

Cost scaling: district base cost inflates with tech/civic tree progress (CostProgressionModel per district, shown where set). Unique civ districts cost half the standard equivalent. 'Specialty' = counts against the population-based district limit (RequiresPopulation).

### Acropolis (unique; replaces Theater Square)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal 1; +2 city strength; unlocked by civic Drama and Poetry
- **Effect:** A district unique to Greece for cultural sites. Replaces the Theater Square district and cheaper to build. Awards 1 Envoy when completed. +1 Culture bonus for adjacent City Center. +1 Culture bonus for each adjacent wonder and district. Can only be built on Hills.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Culture per adjacent wonder | +1 Culture per adjacent district | +1 Culture per adjacent City Center | +1 Culture per adjacent Government Plaza | +2 Culture per adjacent Entertainment Complex | +2 Culture per adjacent Water Park | +2 Culture per adjacent Pamukkale

### Aerodrome
- **Stats:** base cost 54; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal -1; air slots 4; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Flight
- **Effect:** A district that allows you to build and store aircraft. Cannot be built on Hills.

### Aqueduct
- **Stats:** base cost 36; non-specialty; aqueduct-class; unlocked by tech Engineering
- **Effect:** A district that provides this city with a source of fresh water from an adjacent River, Lake, Oasis, or Mountain. Cities that do not yet have existing fresh water receive up to 6 Housing. Cities that already have existing fresh water will instead get +2 Housing. If built adjacent to a Geothermal Fissure +1 Amenity. Prevents Food loss during Drought. Must be built adjacent to the City Center. Military Engineers can spend a charge to complete 20% of an Aqueduct's production.

### Bath (unique; replaces Aqueduct)
- **Stats:** base cost 18; non-specialty; housing +2; amenities +1; aqueduct-class; unlocked by tech Engineering
- **Effect:** A district unique to Rome for city growth. Replaces the Aqueduct district and cheaper to build. It provides this city with a source of fresh water from an adjacent River, Lake, Oasis, or Mountain. Cities that do not yet have existing fresh water receive up to 6 Housing. Cities that already have existing fresh water will instead get +2 Housing. If built adjacent to a Geothermal Fissure +1 Amenity. In all cases the Bath provides an additional bonus of +2 Housing and +1 Amenity. Prevents Food loss during Drought. Must be built adjacent to the City Center. Military Engineers can spend a charge to complete 20% of a Bath's production.

### Campus
- **Stats:** base cost 54; maintenance 1; specialty; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Writing
- **Effect:** A district in your city for scientific endeavors.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Science per adjacent Grassland (Mountain) | +1 Science per adjacent Plains (Mountain) | +1 Science per adjacent Desert (Mountain) | +1 Science per adjacent Tundra (Mountain) | +1 Science per adjacent Snow (Mountain) | +1 Science per 2 adjacent Rainforest | +1 Science per 2 adjacent district | +2 Science per adjacent Great Barrier Reef | +1 Science per adjacent Government Plaza | +2 Science per adjacent Geothermal Fissure | +2 Science per adjacent Reef | +2 Science per adjacent Pamukkale

### Canal
- **Stats:** base cost 81; non-specialty; appeal 1; unlocked by tech Steam Power
- **Effect:** A district built on flat land to connect two bodies of water or a body of water to a City Center. Trade Routes traveling through it can multiply the Gold they get from districts at their destination. Canals may either go straight through the hex or bend by 60 degrees. However three-way Canal junctures are not allowed and Canals must have a full land tile on each side of the waterway they create. Military Engineers can spend a charge to complete 20% of a Canal's production.

### City Center
- **Stats:** base cost 54; non-specialty; air slots 1
- **Effect:** This is the City Center.

### Commercial Hub
- **Stats:** base cost 54; specialty; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Currency
- **Effect:** A district in your city specializing in finance and trade. +1 Trade Route capacity, if this city does not yet have a Harbor district.
- **Adjacency:** +2 Gold per adjacent river | +2 Gold per adjacent Harbor | +2 Gold per adjacent Royal Navy Dockyard | +1 Gold per 2 adjacent district | +1 Gold per adjacent Government Plaza | +2 Gold per adjacent Pamukkale | +2 Gold per adjacent Cothon

### Copacabana (unique; replaces Water Park)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; amenities +2; appeal 1; +2 city strength; must be on coast; unlocked by civic Natural History
- **Effect:** A district unique to Brazil. Replaces the Water Park district, and provides +2 Amenities. Also unlocks the Carnival project, which grants an additional +1 Amenity when underway and a variety of Great People points once completed. Cannot be built in a city with a Street Carnival. Cannot be built on Reef.

### Cothon (unique; replaces Harbor)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; specialty; +2 city strength; must be on coast; unlocked by tech Celestial Navigation
- **Effect:** A district unique to Phoenicia for naval activity in your city. Replaces the Harbor district and cheaper to build. Must be built on Coast or Lake Terrain adjacent to land. +50% Production towards naval units and Settlers in this city. All wounded naval units in this city’s borders heal +100 HP each turn.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Gold per adjacent sea resource | +1 Gold per 2 adjacent district | +2 Gold per adjacent City Center | +1 Gold per adjacent Government Plaza

### Dam
- **Stats:** base cost 81; non-specialty; housing +3; amenities +1; appeal 1; unlocked by tech Buttress
- **Effect:** A district built on a Floodplains tile to improve the comfort of living along this river. Prevents damage from flooding of this river (though yields from flooding drop by 50%). Prevents Food loss during Drought. Only one may be built along each river's floodplain (whichever player completes one first) and the river must traverse at least two sides of the Dam hex. Military Engineers can spend a charge to complete 20% of a Dam's production.

### Diplomatic Quarter
- **Stats:** base cost 30; maintenance 1; specialty; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Mathematics
- **Effect:** Your civilization receives +1 Culture for each Delegation or Embassy from a foreign civilization through diplomacy. +1 Envoy if built next to the city center. Enemy Spies operate at 2 levels below normal targeting this district and adjacent districts. Only 1 can exist in your empire at a time.

### Encampment
- **Stats:** base cost 54; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal -1; +2 city strength; cannot be adjacent to city center; unlocked by tech Bronze Working
- **Effect:** A district in your city for military facilities.

### Entertainment Complex
- **Stats:** base cost 54; maintenance 1; specialty; amenities +1; appeal 1; +2 city strength; unlocked by civic Games and Recreation
- **Effect:** A district in your city dedicated to keeping your people happy by increasing Amenities. Cannot be built in a city with a Water Park.

### Government Plaza
- **Stats:** base cost 30; maintenance 1; specialty; +2 city strength; unlocked by civic State Workforce
- **Effect:** A district placed once in your empire to commemorate your government choices. Provides +8 Loyalty per turn to this city, and an increase of +1 to the adjacency bonuses being earned by any adjacent district. Awards +1 Governor Title.

### Hansa (unique; replaces Industrial Zone)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal -1; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Apprenticeship
- **Effect:** A district unique to Germany for industrial activity. Replaces the Industrial Zone district and cheaper to build. + 2Production bonus for each adjacent Commercial Hub, Aqueduct, Canal, and Dam districts. +1 Production bonus for each adjacent resource. +1 Production bonus for every two adjacent district tiles.
- **Adjacency:** +2 Production per adjacent Commercial Hub | +1 Production per 2 adjacent district | +1 Production per adjacent true | +1 Production per adjacent Government Plaza | +2 Production per adjacent Aqueduct | +2 Production per adjacent Canal | +2 Production per adjacent Dam

### Harbor
- **Stats:** base cost 54; specialty; +2 city strength; must be on coast; unlocked by tech Celestial Navigation
- **Effect:** A district for naval activity in your city. Also removes the Movement penalty for embarking and disembarking to and from this tile. Must be built on Coast or Lake Terrain adjacent to land. +1 Trade Route capacity, if this city does not yet have a Commercial Hub district.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Gold per adjacent sea resource | +1 Gold per 2 adjacent district | +2 Gold per adjacent City Center | +1 Gold per adjacent Government Plaza

### Hippodrome (unique; replaces Entertainment Complex)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; amenities +3; appeal 1; +2 city strength; unlocked by civic Games and Recreation
- **Effect:** A district unique to Byzantium. Replaces the Entertainment Complex district, provides +3 Amenities, and is cheaper to build. When the Hippodrome and buildings in this district are constructed, receive a Heavy Cavalry unit. Units granted from this district do not have a resource maintenance cost. Cannot be built in a city with a Water Park.

### Holy Site
- **Stats:** base cost 54; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal 1; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Astrology
- **Effect:** A district in your city for religious worship.
- **Adjacency:** +2 Faith per adjacent true | +1 Faith per adjacent Grassland (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Plains (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Desert (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Tundra (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Snow (Mountain) | +1 Faith per 2 adjacent Woods | +1 Faith per 2 adjacent district | +1 Faith per adjacent Government Plaza | +1 Faith per adjacent Pamukkale

### Ikanda (unique; replaces Encampment)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; housing +1; appeal -1; +2 city strength; cannot be adjacent to city center; unlocked by tech Bronze Working
- **Effect:** A district unique to Zulu which replaces the Encampment. Provides +1 Housing. Once the Civic or Technology prerequisite is met, Corps and Armies can be built outright. Buildings in the Ikanda receive +2 Gold and +1 Science. Faster Corps and Army creation.

### Industrial Zone
- **Stats:** base cost 54; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal -1; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Apprenticeship
- **Effect:** A district in your city for industrial activity.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Production per adjacent Quarry | +1 Production per 2 adjacent district | +1 Production per adjacent Government Plaza | +1 Production per 2 adjacent Mine | +1 Production per 2 adjacent Lumber Mill | +2 Production per adjacent Aqueduct | +2 Production per adjacent Bath | +2 Production per adjacent Canal | +2 Production per adjacent Dam | +1 Production per adjacent strategic resource

### Lavra (unique; replaces Holy Site)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal 1; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Astrology
- **Effect:** A district unique to Russia for religious activity. Replaces the Holy Site district and cheaper to build. Your city border grows by one tile each time a Great Person is expended in this city. The Lavra provides +1 Great Writer point per turn with a Shrine, +1 Great Artist point per turn with a Temple, and +1 Great Musician point per turn with a Worship building.
- **Adjacency:** +2 Faith per adjacent true | +1 Faith per adjacent Grassland (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Plains (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Desert (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Tundra (Mountain) | +1 Faith per adjacent Snow (Mountain) | +1 Faith per 2 adjacent Woods | +1 Faith per 2 adjacent district | +1 Faith per adjacent Government Plaza | +1 Faith per adjacent Pamukkale

### Mbanza (unique; replaces Neighborhood)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; non-specialty; housing +5; +2 city strength; unlocked by civic Guilds
- **Effect:** A district unique to Kongo that can only be constructed in Rainforest or Woods. Replaces the Neighborhood district but is available earlier and cheaper to build. Provides +5 Housing , +2 Food, and +4 Gold, regardless of Appeal.

### Neighborhood
- **Stats:** base cost 54; non-specialty; housing +4; +2 city strength; unlocked by civic Urbanization
- **Effect:** A district in your city that provides housing based on the Appeal of the tile: Breathtaking: +6 Housing. Charming: +5 Housing. Average: +4 Housing. Uninviting: +3 Housing. Disgusting: +2 Housing.

### Observatory (unique; replaces Campus)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Writing
- **Effect:** A district unique to the Maya for scientific endeavors. Replaces the Campus district and cheaper to build. +2 Science bonus for adjacent Plantations. +1 Science bonus for every two adjacent Farm or district tiles.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Science per 2 adjacent district | +2 Science per adjacent Plantation | +1 Science per 2 adjacent Farm | +2 Science per adjacent Great Barrier Reef | +1 Science per adjacent Government Plaza | +2 Science per adjacent Pamukkale

### Oppidum (unique; replaces Industrial Zone)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; appeal -1; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Iron Working
- **Effect:** A district unique to Gaul that is cheaper and available earlier than the district it replaces, the Industrial Zone. The Oppidum district is defensible with a ranged attack. When the first Oppidum is constructed the Apprenticeship technology is unlocked. +2 Production adjacency bonus from Quarries and strategic resources.
- **Adjacency:** +2 Production per adjacent Quarry | +2 Production per adjacent strategic resource | +1 Production per adjacent Government Plaza

### Preserve
- **Stats:** base cost 54; specialty; housing +1; appeal 1; cannot be adjacent to city center; unlocked by civic Mysticism
- **Effect:** Grants up to 3 Housing based on Appeal. Culture bombs adjacent neutral tiles, and increases their Appeal by 1.

### Royal Navy Dockyard (unique; replaces Harbor)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; specialty; +2 city strength; must be on coast; unlocked by tech Celestial Navigation
- **Effect:** A district unique to England for naval activity in your city. Replaces the Harbor district and cheaper to build. Also removes the Movement penalty for embarking and disembarking to and from this tile. Must be built on Coast or Lake Terrain adjacent to land. +1 Movement for all naval units built in Dockyard +2 Gold when built on a foreign continent +1 Trade Route capacity.
- **Adjacency:** +1 Gold per adjacent sea resource | +1 Gold per 2 adjacent district | +2 Gold per adjacent City Center | +1 Gold per adjacent Government Plaza

### Seowon (unique; replaces Campus)
- **Stats:** base cost 27; maintenance 1; specialty; +2 city strength; unlocked by tech Writing

# Civ VI Full-Anthology Reference — Vol 4: Technology & Civic Trees

<!-- generated by Stage 2 reference build, 2026-08-03 -->
> **Game configuration this volume describes:** RULESET_EXPANSION_2 (Gathering
> Storm ruleset, which includes all Rise & Fall content) + every official DLC
> pack. Optional game modes (Heroes, Secret Societies, Monopolies, Barbarian
> Clans, Apocalypse, Zombies, etc.) are **not** included — the live capture
> calibration shows they are off in this game. Scenario-only content excluded.
>
> **Sourcing:** every value is machine-extracted from the game's own data files
> (base + Expansion1 + Expansion2 XML and each DLC pack's Data XML, merged in
> the game's modinfo-declared load order). Nothing comes from model memory.
> Verified against the live game DB: 36 districts (26 specialty), 54 resources
> (34 luxuries), 7 victories, 8 governors / 48 promotions — all exact matches.
>
> **Trust order if something disagrees:** 1) the live snapshot from the
> tracker, 2) this document, 3) anything else. Mods (e.g. Real Strategy) can
> shift values; the live snapshot always wins.

Boosts (eurekas) give the listed percentage of the tech's cost (standard is 40% in the expansions; per-boost value shown).

# Civ VI Full-Anthology Reference — Vol 5: Governments, Policies, Governors, Religion & Great People

<!-- generated by Stage 2 reference build, 2026-08-03 -->
> **Game configuration this volume describes:** RULESET_EXPANSION_2 (Gathering
> Storm ruleset, which includes all Rise & Fall content) + every official DLC
> pack. Optional game modes (Heroes, Secret Societies, Monopolies, Barbarian
> Clans, Apocalypse, Zombies, etc.) are **not** included — the live capture
> calibration shows they are off in this game. Scenario-only content excluded.
>
> **Sourcing:** every value is machine-extracted from the game's own data files
> (base + Expansion1 + Expansion2 XML and each DLC pack's Data XML, merged in
> the game's modinfo-declared load order). Nothing comes from model memory.
> Verified against the live game DB: 36 districts (26 specialty), 54 resources
> (34 luxuries), 7 victories, 8 governors / 48 promotions — all exact matches.
>
> **Trust order if something disagrees:** 1) the live snapshot from the
> tracker, 2) this document, 3) anything else. Mods (e.g. Real Strategy) can
> shift values; the live snapshot always wins.

## Governments

### Chiefdom
- **Stats:** slots: 1 military, 1 economic; 1 influence pts/turn (envoy at 100); +0 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** No Bonus.
- **Legacy bonus:** No Bonus.

### Autocracy
- **Stats:** slots: 1 military, 1 economic, 1 diplomatic, 1 wildcard; unlocked by Political Philosophy; 3 influence pts/turn (envoy at 100); +1 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +1 to all yields for each government building and palace in a city.
- **Legacy bonus:** +10% Production toward Wonders.

### Classical Republic
- **Stats:** slots: 2 economic, 1 diplomatic, 1 wildcard; unlocked by Political Philosophy; 3 influence pts/turn (envoy at 100); +1 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** All cities with a district receive +1 Housing and +1 Amenity.
- **Legacy bonus:** +15% Great Person points.

### Oligarchy
- **Stats:** slots: 2 military, 1 economic, 1 wildcard; unlocked by Political Philosophy; 3 influence pts/turn (envoy at 100); +1 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** All land melee, anti-cavalry, and naval melee class units gain +4 Combat Strength.
- **Legacy bonus:** +20% Unit Experience.

### Merchant Republic
- **Stats:** slots: 1 military, 2 economic, 2 diplomatic, 1 wildcard; unlocked by Exploration; 5 influence pts/turn (envoy at 150); +2 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +10% Gold in all cities with an established Governor.
- **Legacy bonus:** +15% Production toward Districts.

### Monarchy
- **Stats:** slots: 2 military, 1 economic, 1 diplomatic, 2 wildcard; unlocked by Divine Right; 5 influence pts/turn (envoy at 150); +2 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +1 Housing per level of Walls. +2 Diplomatic Favor for every Renaissance Wall.
- **Legacy bonus:** +50% Influence Points.

### Theocracy
- **Stats:** slots: 2 military, 2 economic, 1 diplomatic, 1 wildcard; unlocked by Reformed Church; 5 influence pts/turn (envoy at 150); +2 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +5 Religious Strength in Theological Combat. +0.5 Faith per Citizen in cities with Governors.
- **Legacy bonus:** 15% Discount on Purchases with Faith.

### Communism
- **Stats:** slots: 3 military, 3 economic, 1 diplomatic, 1 wildcard; unlocked by Class Struggle; 7 influence pts/turn (envoy at 200); +3 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +0.6 Production per Citizen in cities with Governors.
- **Legacy bonus:** +10% Science.

### Democracy
- **Stats:** slots: 1 military, 3 economic, 2 diplomatic, 2 wildcard; unlocked by Suffrage; 7 influence pts/turn (envoy at 200); +3 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** Your Trade Routes to an Ally or Suzerain's city provide +4 Food and +4 Production for both cities. Alliance Points with all allies increase by an additional .25 per turn.
- **Legacy bonus:** 15% Discount on Purchases with Gold.

### Fascism
- **Stats:** slots: 4 military, 1 economic, 1 diplomatic, 2 wildcard; unlocked by Totalitarianism; 7 influence pts/turn (envoy at 200); +3 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** All units gain +5 Combat Strength. War Weariness reduced by 15%.
- **Legacy bonus:** +50% Production toward Units.

### Corporate Libertarianism
- **Stats:** slots: 3 military, 1 economic, 1 diplomatic, 5 wildcard; unlocked by Venture Politics; 9 influence pts/turn (envoy at 250); +4 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** Commercial Hubs and Encampments provide cities with +10% Production, and accumulating resources with improvements provide +1 per turn.
- **Legacy bonus:** -10% Science.

### Digital Democracy
- **Stats:** slots: 1 military, 1 economic, 3 diplomatic, 5 wildcard; unlocked by Distributed Sovereignty; 9 influence pts/turn (envoy at 250); +4 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +2 Amenities in all cities, and +2 Culture per Specialty District.
- **Legacy bonus:** -3 Combat Strength for all units.

### Synthetic Technocracy
- **Stats:** slots: 1 military, 3 economic, 1 diplomatic, 5 wildcard; unlocked by Optimization Imperative; 9 influence pts/turn (envoy at 250); +4 Diplomatic Favor/turn
- **Inherent bonus:** +3 Power in all cities, and +30% Production towards all city projects.
- **Legacy bonus:** -10% Tourism.


## Policy cards

Grouped by slot type. Each card lists its unlocking civic (or tech) and obsolescence where defined.

### Military — 40 cards

- **After Action Reports** [Rapid Deployment]: All units gain +25% combat experience.
- **Agoge** [Craftsmanship]: +50% Production toward Ancient and Classical era melee, anti-cavalry, and ranged units.
- **Bastions** [Defensive Tactics]: +6 City Defense Strength. +5 City Ranged Strength.
- **Chivalry** [Divine Right]: +50% Production toward Industrial era and earlier heavy and light cavalry units.
- **Conscription** [State Workforce]: Unit maintenance reduced by 1 Gold per turn, per unit.
- **Defense of the Motherland** [Class Struggle; exclusive to Communism]: No war weariness from combat in your territory.
- **Discipline** [Code of Laws]: +5 Unit Combat Strength when fighting Barbarians.
- **Drill Manuals** [Mercantilism]: All improved Niter and Coal resources yield 1 additional resource per turn.
- **Equestrian Orders** [Military Training]: All improved Horses and Iron resources yield 1 additional resource per turn.
- **Feudal Contract** [Feudalism]: +50% Production toward Ancient, Classical, Medieval, and Renaissance era melee, anti-cavalry, and ranged units.
- **Force Modernization** [Urbanization]: 50% Gold and resource discount on all unit upgrades.
- **Grande Armée** [Nationalism]: +50% Production toward Industrial era and earlier melee, anti-cavalry, and ranged units.
- **Integrated Space Cell** [Space Race]: +15% Production toward Space Race projects if a city has either a Military Academy or a Seaport.
- **International Waters** [Cold War]: +100% Production toward all naval units, excluding Carriers.
- **Levée en Masse** [Mobilization]: Unit maintenance cost reduced by 2 Gold per turn, per unit.
- **Lightning Warfare** [Totalitarianism]: +50% Production for all heavy and light cavalry units.
- **Limes** [Defensive Tactics]: +100% Production toward defensive buildings.
- **Limitanei** [Early Empire]: +2 Loyalty per turn for cities with a garrisoned unit.
- **Logistics** [Mercantilism]: +1 Movement if starting turn in friendly territory.
- **Maneuver** [Military Tradition]: +50% Production toward Ancient and Classical era heavy and light cavalry units.
- **Maritime Industries** [Foreign Trade]: +100% Production toward Ancient and Classical era naval units.
- **Martial Law** [Totalitarianism; exclusive to Fascism]: Accumulate 25% less war weariness than usual. +2 Loyalty per turn for cities with a garrisoned unit.
- **Military First** [Rapid Deployment]: +50% Production toward all melee, anti-cavalry, and ranged units.
- **Military Research** [Urbanization]: Military Academies, Seaports, and Renaissance Walls generate +2 Science.
- **National Identity** [Nationalism]: Units have 50% less Combat Strength reduction from being injured.
- **Native Conquest** [Colonialism]: Combat victories over units from earlier eras provide Gold equal to 50% of the Combat Strength of the defeated unit. (on Standard Speed)
- **Press Gangs** [Exploration]: 100% Production toward Industrial era and earlier naval units.
- **Professional Army** [Mercenaries]: 50% discount on all unit upgrades.
- **Propaganda** [Mass Media]: Accumulate 25% less war weariness than usual.
- **Raid** [Military Training]: Yields gained from pillaging and coastal raids are +50%.
- **Retainers** [Civil Service]: +1 Amenity for cities with a garrisoned unit.
- **Retinues** [Mercenaries]: 50% resource discount on all unit upgrades.
- **Sack** [Mercenaries]: Yields gained from pillaging are doubled for pillaging districts.
- **Second Strike Capability** [Cold War]: Nuclear Device maintenance reduced by 50% Gold per turn.
- **Strategic Air Force** [Globalization]: +50% Production toward all air units and toward Carriers.
- **Survey** [Code of Laws]: Double experience for recon units.
- **Their Finest Hour** [Suffrage; exclusive to Democracy]: +50% Production toward Modern and Atomic air units.
- **Total War** [Scorched Earth]: Yields gained from pillaging, coastal raids, and plundering Trade Routes are +50%.
- **Veterancy** [Military Training]: +30% Production toward Encampment districts and buildings for that district.
- **Wars of Religion** [Reformed Church]: +4 Combat Strength when a non-religious unit fights a civilization that follows another Religion.

### Economic — 45 cards

- **Aesthetics** [Medieval Faires]: +100% Theater Square district adjacency bonuses.
- **Caravansaries** [Foreign Trade]: +2 Gold from all Trade Routes.
- **Civil Prestige** [Civil Service]: Established Governors with at least 2 Promotions provide +1 Amenity and +2 Housing.
- **Collectivization** [Class Struggle; exclusive to Communism]: +4 Food from domestic Trade Routes.
- **Colonial Offices** [Exploration]: +15% faster growth and 3 Loyalty per turn for cities not on your original Capital's continent.
- **Colonial Taxes** [Colonialism]: +25% Gold and +10% Production in cities not on your original Capital's continent.
- **Colonization** [Early Empire]: +50% Production toward Settlers.
- **Corvée** [State Workforce]: +15% Production toward Ancient and Classical wonders.
- **Craftsmen** [Guilds]: 100% Industrial Zone adjacency bonuses.
- **Ecommerce** [Globalization]: +2 Production and +5 Gold from all Trade Routes.
- **Economic Union** [Suffrage]: +100% Commercial Hub and Harbor district adjacency bonuses.
- **Expropriation** [Scorched Earth]: +50% Production toward Settlers. Plot purchase cost reduced by 20%.
- **Five-Year Plan** [Class Struggle]: +100% Campus and Industrial Zone district adjacency bonuses.
- **Free Market** [The Enlightenment]: Extra Gold from buildings in Commercial Hubs: +50% if city population is 15 or higher, +50% if district has at least +4 adjacency bonus.
- **God King** [Code of Laws]: +1 Faith and +1 Gold in the Capital.
- **Gothic Architecture** [Divine Right]: +15% Production toward Renaissance, Medieval, Classical, and Ancient wonders.
- **Grand Opera** [Opera and Ballet]: Extra Culture from buildings in Theater Squares: +50% if city population is 15 or higher, +50% if district has at least +4 adjacency bonus.
- **Heritage Tourism** [Cultural Heritage]: +100% Tourism from Great Works of Art and Artifacts.
- **Ilkum** [Craftsmanship]: +30% Production toward Builders.
- **Insulae** [Games and Recreation]: +1 Housing in all cities with at least 2 specialty districts.
- **Land Surveyors** [Early Empire]: Reduces the cost of purchasing a tile by 20%.
- **Liberalism** [The Enlightenment]: +1 Amenity to all cities with at least 2 specialty districts.
- **Market Economy** [Capitalism]: Your international Trade Routes provide +1 Gold per Luxury and Strategic resource improved at the destination, as well as +2 Culture and +2 Science.
- **Medina Quarter** [Medieval Faires]: +2 Housing in all cities with at least 3 specialty districts.
- **Meritocracy** [Civil Service]: Each city receives +1 Culture for each specialty district it constructs.
- **Natural Philosophy** [Recorded History]: +100% Campus district adjacency bonuses.
- **Naval Infrastructure** [Naval Tradition]: +100% Harbor district adjacency bonuses.
- **New Deal** [Suffrage; exclusive to Democracy]: +4 Housing, +2 Amenities, -8 Gold to all cities with at least 3 specialty districts.
- **Online Communities** [Social Media]: +50% Tourism output to civilizations to which you have a Trade Route.
- **Public Transport** [Urbanization]: Receive 100 Gold per Appeal of tile when replacing a Farm with a Neighborhood district.
- **Public Works** [Civil Engineering]: +30% Production toward Builders, and newly trained Builders gain 2 extra build actions.
- **Rationalism** [The Enlightenment]: Extra Science from buildings in Campuses: +50% if city population is 15 or higher, +50% if district has at least +4 adjacency bonus.
- **Religious Orders** [Reformed Church]: All Religious units +5 Religious Strength in theological combat.
- **Resource Management** [Conservation]: 1 copy of a Strategic resource allows you to produce and purchase units requiring it in any city.
- **Satellite Broadcasts** [Space Race]: +200% Tourism from Great Works of Music.
- **Scripture** [Theology]: +100% Holy Site adjacency bonuses.
- **Serfdom** [Feudalism]: Newly trained Builders gain 2 extra build actions.
- **Simultaneum** [Reformed Church]: Extra Faith from buildings in Holy Sites: +50% if city population is 15 or higher, +50% if district has at least +4 adjacency bonus.
- **Skyscrapers** [Civil Engineering]: +15% Production toward all wonders.
- **Sports Media** [Professional Sports]: +100% Theater Square district adjacency bonuses, and Stadiums generate +1 Amenity.
- **Third Alternative** [Totalitarianism; exclusive to Fascism]: +4 Gold from each Research Lab, Military Academy, and Power Plant.
- **Town Charters** [Guilds]: +100% Commercial Hub district adjacency bonuses.
- **Trade Confederation** [Mercenaries]: +1 Culture and +1 Science from international Trade Routes.
- **Triangular Trade** [Mercantilism]: +4 Gold and +1 Faith from all Trade Routes.
- **Urban Planning** [Code of Laws]: +1 Production in all cities.

### Diplomatic — 15 cards

- **Charismatic Leader** [Political Philosophy]: +2 Influence points per turn toward earning city-state Envoys.
- **Collective Activism** [Social Media]: +5% Culture per city-state you are the Suzerain of.
- **Communications Office** [Social Media]: Governors provide +1 Loyalty per turn to their city, per Promotion the Governor has.
- **Containment** [Cold War]: Each Envoy you send to a city-state counts as two, if its Suzerain has a different government than you.
- **Cryptography** [Cold War]: Enemy Spy level reduced by 2 in your lands. Your Spy level is increased by 1 for offensive operations.
- **Diplomatic League** [Political Philosophy]: The first Envoy you send to each city-state counts as two Envoys.
- **Gunboat Diplomacy** [Totalitarianism]: Open Borders with all city-states, and +4 Influence points per turn toward earning Envoys.
- **International Space Agency** [Globalization]: +5% Science per city-state you are the Suzerain of.
- **Machiavellianism** [Diplomatic Service]: +50% Production toward Spies. Spy operations take 25% less time.
- **Merchant Confederation** [Medieval Faires]: +1 Gold from each of your Envoys at city-states.
- **Music Censorship** [Space Race]: Rock Bands from other players may not enter your territory. -1 Amenity in all of your cities with 10 or more Population.
- **Nuclear Espionage** [Nuclear Program]: Spies who steal a tech boost without being detected gain an extra boost.
- **Praetorium** [Recorded History]: Governors provide +2 Loyalty per turn to their city.
- **Raj** [Colonialism]: +2 Science, Culture, Faith, and Gold from each city-state you are Suzerain of.
- **Wisselbanken** [Diplomatic Service]: Your Trade Routes to an Ally's city or vassal city-state provide +2 Food and +2 Production for both cities. Alliance Points with all allies increase by an additional .25 per turn.

### Wildcard — 30 cards

- **Aerospace Contractors** [Exodus Imperative]: Cities with a Spaceport gain +3 Aluminum per turn and +3 Power.
- **Autocratic Legacy**: +1 to all yields for each government building and palace in a city.
- **Automated Workforce**: Your cities get +20% Production towards city projects. BUT: -1 Amenity and -5 Loyalty per turn in your cities.
- **Collectivism**: Farms +1 Food. All cities +2 Housing. +100% Industrial Zone adjacency bonuses. BUT: Great People Points earned 50% slower.
- **Communist Legacy**: +0.6 Production per Citizen in cities with Governors.
- **Cyber Warfare**: +10 Combat Strength against units from the Information and Future Eras. BUT: Grievances against you do not decay.
- **Democratic Legacy**: Your Trade Routes to an Ally or Suzerain's city provide +4 Food and +4 Production for both cities. Alliance Points with all allies increase by an additional .25 per turn.
- **Diplomatic Capital** [Smart Power Doctrine]: +4 Diplomatic Favor per turn.
- **Disinformation Campaign**: +3 Diplomatic Favor per turn for each Broadcast Center. BUT: -10% Science and Culture in all cities.
- **Elite Forces**: +100% combat experience for all units. BUT: +2 Gold to maintain each combat and spy unit.
- **Fascist Legacy**: All units gain +5 Combat Strength. War Weariness reduced by 15%.
- **Flower Power**: All Civilizations not currently at war receive +100% of the Tourism from your Concerts. BUT: The cost of producing is decreased by 100% and purchasing is +100% for units other than Rock Bands..
- **Global Coalition** [Smart Power Doctrine]: +7 Combat Strength for units in friendly territory.
- **Hallyu** [Cultural Hegemony]: Your Rock Band units can choose from any possible promotion.
- **Inquisition**: Start Inquisition with 1 Apostle charge. All Religious units +15 Religious Combat Strength in friendly territory. BUT: -25% Science in all cities.
- **Integrated Attack Logistics** [Information Warfare]: +1 Movement if starting turn in enemy territory. +50% Production for Giant Death Robots.
- **Isolationism**: Domestic routes provide +2 Food, +2 Production. BUT: Can't train or buy Settlers nor settle new cities.
- **Letters of Marque**: Naval Raiders: +100% Production, +2 Movement. Yields doubled from plundering Trade Routes. BUT: Trade Route yields -50%.
- **Mercantile Legacy**: +10% Gold in all cities with an established Governor.
- **Monarchic Legacy**: +1 Housing per level of Walls. +2 Diplomatic Favor for every Renaissance Wall.
- **Monasticism**: +75% Science in cities with a Holy Site. BUT: -25% Culture in all cities.
- **Non-State Actors** [Cultural Hegemony]: Your Spy units can choose from any possible promotion.
- **Oligarchic Legacy**: All land melee, anti-cavalry, and naval melee class units gain +4 Combat Strength.
- **Rabblerousing** [Information Warfare]: When you reduce a player's Diplomatic Victory points in the World Congress, get 50% of your spent Diplomatic Favor back. +1 Diplomatic Favor per turn.
- **Republican Legacy**: All cities with a district receive +1 Housing and +1 Amenity.
- **Robber Barons**: +50% Gold in cities with a Stock Exchange. +25% Production in cities with a Factory. BUT: -2 Amenities in all cities.
- **Rogue State**: +50% Production to nuclear program projects and Nuclear Devices. BUT: Earn no influence toward new Envoys.
- **Space Tourism** [Exodus Imperative]: Tourism from other players is reduced by 20% versus your civilization.
- **Theocratic Legacy**: +5 Religious Strength in Theological Combat. +0.5 Faith per Citizen in cities with Governors.
- **Twilight Valor**: +5 Combat Strength for all melee attack units. BUT: Cannot heal outside your territory.

## Governors (8) and promotions (48)

### Victor — The Castellan
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 150
- **Base ability:** Military focused, once established in a city, Victor is instrumental in strengthening, preserving, and defending it from foreign threats.
- **Redoubt** (level 0 — BASE): Increases city garrison Combat Strength by +5. Establishes in 3 turns.
- **Garrison Commander** (level 1) (requires Redoubt): Units defending within the city's territory get +5 Combat Strength. Your other cities within 9 tiles gain +4 Loyalty per turn towards your civilization.
- **Defense Logistics** (level 1) (requires Redoubt): City cannot be put under siege. Accumulating Strategic resources in the city gain an additional +1 per turn.
- **Embrasure** (level 2) (requires Defense Logistics, Garrison Commander): City gains an additional Ranged Strike per turn. Military units trained in this city start with a free promotion that do not already start with a free promotion.
- **Air Defense Initiative** (level 3) (requires Embrasure): +25 Combat Strength to anti-air support units within the city's territory when defending against aircraft and ICBMs.
- **Arms Race Proponent** (level 3) (requires Embrasure): 30% Production increase to all nuclear armament projects in the city.

### Amani — The Diplomat
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 100
- **Base ability:** Skilled in gaining support for your civilization, and spreading its influence to nearby cities. Amani is the only governor that can be given foreign assignment in a city-state.
- **Messenger** (level 0 — BASE): Can be assigned to a city-state, where she acts as 2 Envoys.
- **Emissary** (level 1) (requires Messenger): Other cities within 9 tiles and not owned by you lose 2 Loyalty per turn.
- **Local Informants** (level 2) (requires Emissary): Enemy Spies operate at 3 levels below normal in this city.
- **Affluence** (level 1) (requires Messenger): While established in a city-state, provides a copy of its Luxury resources to you.
- **Foreign Investor** (level 2) (requires Affluence): While established in a city-state, accumulate its Strategic resources. When suzerain receive double the amount of accumulated strategic resources.
- **Puppeteer** (level 3) (requires Local Informants, Foreign Investor): While established in a city-state, doubles the number of Envoys you have there.

### Moksha — The Cardinal
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 100
- **Base ability:** Spiritual and Religious leader that can increase the Religious Strength of a city, and the Religious units stationed there. Moksha is a beacon of Faith in your empire.
- **Bishop** (level 0 — BASE): Religious pressure to adjacent cities is 100% stronger from this city. +2 Faith for every specialty district in this city.
- **Grand Inquisitor** (level 1) (requires Bishop): +10 Religious Strength in theological combat in tiles of this city.
- **Laying On Of Hands** (level 1) (requires Bishop): All Governor's units heal fully in one turn in tiles of this city.
- **Citadel of God** (level 2) (requires Grand Inquisitor, Laying On Of Hands): City ignores religious pressure from Religions not founded by the Governor's player. Gain Faith equal to 25% of the construction cost when finishing buildings.
- **Patron Saint** (level 3) (requires Citadel of God): Apostles and Warrior Monks trained in the city receive 1 extra promotion when receiving their first promotion.
- **Divine Architect** (level 3) (requires Citadel of God): Allows city to purchase districts with Faith.

### Magnus — The Steward
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 100
- **Base ability:** Enterprising and capable, Magnus is able to procure valuable resources when needed. He is also quite skilled in optimizing the overall Production in the city.
- **Groundbreaker** (level 0 — BASE): +50% yields from plot harvests and feature removals in city.
- **Surplus Logistics** (level 1) (requires Groundbreaker): +20% Growth in the city. Your Trade Routes ending here provide +2 Food to their starting city.
- **Provision** (level 1) (requires Groundbreaker): Settlers trained in the city do not consume a Population.
- **Industrialist** (level 2) (requires Surplus Logistics): Increases the Power provided by each resource of the Coal Power Plant, Oil Power Plant, and Nuclear Power Plant by 1 and the Production by +2.
- **Black Marketeer** (level 2) (requires Provision): Strategic resource costs for units are discounted 80%.
- **Vertical Integration** (level 3) (requires Industrialist, Black Marketeer): This city receives Production from all nearby Industrial Zone buildings with regional bonuses, not just the first.

### Liang — The Surveyor
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 100
- **Base ability:** An expert in efficiency, Liang is skilled in all things related to building and construction. An expert planner, she can also supervise the development of custom improvements in the city.
- **Guildmaster** (level 0 — BASE): All Builders trained in this city will get +1 build charge.
- **Zoning Commissioner** (level 1) (requires Guildmaster): +20% Production towards constructing districts in the city.
- **Aquaculture** (level 1) (requires Guildmaster): Can construct the Fishery improvement. +1 Food, +0.5 Housing, +1 Food if adjacent to a sea resource. +1 Production if Liang is in the city.
- **Reinforced Materials** (level 2) (requires Zoning Commissioner): This city’s improvements, buildings, and districts cannot be damaged by Environmental Effects.
- **Water Works** (level 2) (requires Aquaculture): +2 Housing for every Neighborhood and Aqueduct district in this city. +1 Amenity for every Canal and Dam district in this city.
- **Parks and Recreation** (level 3) (requires Water Works, Reinforced Materials): Can construct the City Park improvement in this city. +1 Culture and +2 Appeal. +1 Amenity if adjacent to water. City Parks provide +3 Culture if Liang is in the city.

### Pingala — The Educator
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 100
- **Base ability:** Pingala is focused on the cultivation of Scientific and Cultural endeavors in the city. He is also quite skilled in the attraction of Great People to his city.
- **Librarian** (level 0 — BASE): 15% increase in Science and Culture generated by the city.
- **Connoisseur** (level 1) (requires Librarian): +1 Culture per turn for each Citizen in the city.
- **Researcher** (level 1) (requires Librarian): +1 Science per turn for each Citizen in the city.
- **Grants** (level 2) (requires Connoisseur, Researcher): +100% Great People points generated per turn in the city.
- **Curator** (level 3) (requires Grants): +100% Tourism from Great Works of Art, Music, and Writing in the city.
- **Space Initiative** (level 3) (requires Grants): 30% Production increase to all space-program projects in the city.

### Reyna — The Financier
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 100
- **Base ability:** Shrewd and fiscally knowledgeable, Reyna is able to strengthen the economic power of a city, using finances to provide more than is normally possible.
- **Land Acquisition** (level 0 — BASE): Acquire new tiles in city faster. +3 Gold per turn from each foreign Trade Route passing through the city.
- **Harbormaster** (level 1) (requires Land Acquisition): Double adjacency bonuses from Commercial Hubs and Harbors in the city.
- **Forestry Management** (level 1) (requires Land Acquisition): This city receives +2 Gold from each unimproved feature. Tiles adjacent to unimproved features receive +1 Appeal in this city.
- **Tax Collector** (level 2) (requires Harbormaster, Forestry Management): +2 Gold per turn for each Citizen in the city.
- **Renewable Subsidizer** (level 3) (requires Tax Collector): All Offshore Wind Farms, Solar Farms, Wind Farms, Geothermal Plants, and Hydroelectric Dams in this city receive +2 Power and +2 Gold.
- **Contractor** (level 3) (requires Tax Collector): Allows city to purchase districts with Gold.

### Ibrahim — The Grand Vizier
- **Stats:** identity pressure 8; turns to establish 150
- **Base ability:** Suleiman's vizier Ibrahim, is a Military and Diplomacy focused governor. In addition to having a unique promotion tree, Ibrahim is the only Governor that can be assigned to another civilization's capital as well as any domestic city. He is well suited for influencing military operations but is also a skilled diplomat, strengthening relationships with friendly civilizations and easing tensions with rivals.
- **Pasha** (level 0 — BASE): +20% Production to all military units in the city.
- **Head Falconer** (level 1) (requires Pasha): All friendly units fighting within the city's territory gain +5 Combat Strength.
- **Serasker** (level 1) (requires Pasha): Grants all units within 10 tiles of the City Center +10 Combat Strength when attacking defensible districts.
- **Khass-Oda-Bashi** (level 2) (requires Head Falconer): When established in an allied foreign Capital, your Alliance Points with the owner increase an extra .5 per turn.
- **Capou Agha** (level 2) (requires Serasker): When established in a foreign Capital, Grievances from the city owner against you are reduced by 1 more per turn.
- **Grand Vizier** (level 3) (requires Khass-Oda-Bashi, Capou Agha): When established in a foreign Capital, none of the owner's cities exert Loyalty pressure on your cities.


## Religion

### Beliefs — 59 total, by class

#### Pantheon (23)

- **City Patron Goddess:** +25% Production toward districts in cities without a specialty district.
- **Dance of the Aurora:** Holy Site districts get +1 Faith from adjacent Tundra tiles.
- **Desert Folklore:** Holy Site districts get +1 Faith from adjacent Desert tiles.
- **Divine Spark:** +1 Great Person point from Holy Site (Prophet), Campus (Scientist), and Theater Square (Writer) districts.
- **Earth Goddess:** +1 Faith from tiles with Charming or better Appeal.
- **Fertility Rites:** City growth rate is 10% higher.
- **Fire Goddess:** +2 Faith from Geothermal Fissures and Volcanic Soil.
- **God of Craftsmen:** +1 Production from Mines over Strategic resources.
- **God of Healing:** Increases Healing by +30 in your Holy Site district, or any adjacent tiles.
- **God of War:** Bonus Faith equal to 50% of the strength of each combat unit killed within 8 tiles of a Holy Site district. (on Standard Speed)
- **God of the Forge:** +25% Production toward Ancient and Classical military units.
- **God of the Open Sky:** +1 Culture from Pastures.
- **God of the Sea:** +1 Production from Fishing Boats.
- **Goddess of Festivals:** +1 Food from Wine, Incense, Cocoa, Tobacco, Olives, Coffee, and Tea Plantations.
- **Goddess of the Hunt:** +1 Food from Camps.
- **Initiation Rites:** +50 Faith for each Barbarian Outpost dispersed.
- **Lady of the Reeds and Marshes:** +1 Production from Marsh, Oasis, and Floodplains.
- **Monument to the Gods:** +15% Production towards Ancient and Classical era wonders.
- **Religious Idols:** +2 Faith from Mines over Luxury and Bonus resources.
- **Religious Settlements:** Border expansion rate is 15% higher.
- **River Goddess:** +1 Amenity to cities if they have a Holy Site district adjacent to a River.
- **Sacred Path:** Holy Site districts get +1 Faith from adjacent Rainforest tiles.
- **Stone Circles:** +2 Faith from Quarries.

#### Founder (9)

- **Cross-Cultural Dialogue:** +1 Science for every 5 followers of this Religion in other civilizations.
- **Lay Ministry:** Each Holy Site or Theater Square district in a city following this Religion provides +1 Faith or +1 Culture respectively.
- **Papal Primacy:** When you send an Envoy to a City-State it adds 200 Religious pressure to that City-State.
- **Pilgrimage:** +2 Faith for every city following this Religion in other civilizations and City-States.
- **Religious Unity:** +1 Envoy at each City-State when it first adopts this Religion, in addition to any envoy from a City-State quest.
- **Sacred Places:** +2 Science, Culture, Gold, and Faith for each city following this Religion that has a World Wonder.
- **Stewardship:** Each Campus or Commercial Hub district in a city following this Religion provides +1 Science or +1 Gold respectively.
- **Tithe:** +1 Gold for every 4 followers of this Religion.
- **World Church:** +1 Culture for every 5 followers of this Religion in other civilizations.

#### Follower (9)

- **Choral Music:** Shrines and Temples provide Culture equal to their intrinsic Faith output.
- **Divine Inspiration:** All world wonders provide +4 Faith.
- **Feed the World:** Shrines and Temples provide Food equal to their intrinsic Faith output.
- **Jesuit Education:** May purchase Campus and Theater Square district buildings with Faith.
- **Religious Community:** Shrines and Temples each provide +1 Housing.
- **Reliquaries:** Relics have triple yield of both Faith and Tourism.
- **Warrior Monks:** Allows spending Faith to train Warrior Monks, medieval land combat units with a unique promotion tree. May only be purchased in a city with a Temple in its Holy Site.
- **Work Ethic:** +1% Production for each citizen following this religion in the city.
- **Zen Meditation:** +1 Amenity in cities with 2 specialty districts.

#### Enhancer (9)

- **Crusade:** Combat units gain +10 Combat Strength when within the borders of foreign cities that follow this Religion.
- **Defender of the Faith:** Combat units gain +5 Combat Strength when within the borders of friendly cities that follow this Religion.
- **Holy Order:** Missionaries and Apostles are 30% cheaper to purchase.
- **Holy Waters:** Increases Healing of your religious units by +10 in Holy Site districts belonging to cities with your majority religion, or any adjacent tiles.
- **Itinerant Preachers:** Religion spreads to cities 30% further away.
- **Missionary Zeal:** Religious units ignore Movement costs of terrain and features.
- **Monastic Isolation:** Your Religion's pressure never drops due to losses in Theological Combat.
- **Religious Colonization:** Cities start with this Religion in place if founded by a player who has this as their majority Religion.
- **Scripture:** Religious spread from adjacent city pressure is 25% stronger. Boosted to 50% once Printing is researched.

#### Worship (9)

- **Cathedral:** Allows construction of Cathedrals (+3 Faith, 1 slot for religious art).
- **Dar-e Mehr:** Allows construction of Dar-e Mehrs (+3 Faith, +1 additional for each era since constructed or last repaired).
- **Gurdwara:** Allows construction of Gurdwaras (+3 Faith, +2 Food).
- **Meeting House:** Allows construction of Meeting Houses (+3 Faith, +2 Production).
- **Mosque:** Allows construction of Mosques (+3 Faith). Missionaries and Apostles +1 Spread.
- **Pagoda:** Allows construction of Pagodas (+3 Faith, +1 Housing).
- **Stupa:** Allows construction of Stupas (+3 Faith, +1 Amenity).
- **Synagogue:** Allows construction of Synagogues (+5 Faith).
- **Wat:** Allows construction of Wats (+3 Faith, +2 Science).

### Religions available to found: 24 named religions (name choice is cosmetic; a custom name is also allowed).

# Civ VI Full-Anthology Reference — Vol 6: Units, Resources & Improvements

<!-- generated by Stage 2 reference build, 2026-08-03 -->
> **Game configuration this volume describes:** RULESET_EXPANSION_2 (Gathering
> Storm ruleset, which includes all Rise & Fall content) + every official DLC
> pack. Optional game modes (Heroes, Secret Societies, Monopolies, Barbarian
> Clans, Apocalypse, Zombies, etc.) are **not** included — the live capture
> calibration shows they are off in this game. Scenario-only content excluded.
>
> **Sourcing:** every value is machine-extracted from the game's own data files
> (base + Expansion1 + Expansion2 XML and each DLC pack's Data XML, merged in
> the game's modinfo-declared load order). Nothing comes from model memory.
> Verified against the live game DB: 36 districts (26 specialty), 54 resources
> (34 luxuries), 7 victories, 8 governors / 48 promotions — all exact matches.
>
> **Trust order if something disagrees:** 1) the live snapshot from the
> tracker, 2) this document, 3) anything else. Mods (e.g. Real Strategy) can
> shift values; the live snapshot always wins.

## Units — 144 total

CS = melee combat strength, RS = ranged strength. GS strategic-resource rules: 'costs N <resource>' is the one-time creation cost from your stockpile; 'upkeep' is per-turn resource consumption where defined. Unique units are also listed under their civilization in Vols 1–2.
