# Civ VI Full-Anthology Reference — Vol 7: Expansion Mechanics (Loyalty, Ages, Alliances, Emergencies, Favor, Congress, Climate, Power)

<!-- generated by Stage 2 reference build, 2026-08-03 -->
> **Game configuration this volume describes:** RULESET_EXPANSION_2 (Gathering
> Storm ruleset, which includes all Rise & Fall content) + every official DLC
> pack. Optional game modes (Heroes, Secret Societies, Monopolies, Barbarian
> Clans, Apocalypse, Zombies, etc.) are **not** included — the live capture
> calibration shows they are off in this game. Scenario-only content excluded.
>
> **Sourcing:** every value is machine-extracted from the game's own data files
> (base + Expansion1 + Expansion2 XML and each DLC pack's Data XML, merged in
> the game's modinfo-declared load order). Nothing comes from model memory.
> Verified against the live game DB: 36 districts (26 specialty), 54 resources
> (34 luxuries), 7 victories, 8 governors / 48 promotions — all exact matches.
>
> **Trust order if something disagrees:** 1) the live snapshot from the
> tracker, 2) this document, 3) anything else. Mods (e.g. Real Strategy) can
> shift values; the live snapshot always wins.

## Loyalty & cultural identity (Rise & Fall system, active under GS)

Cities start at 100 loyalty, maximum 100. Per-turn loyalty pressure from nearby citizens: each citizen within 10 tiles exerts identity pressure (base 1 per citizen, 1 extra for capitals); pressure scales with age bonuses (Golden +1.5, normal +1.0, Dark +0.5 multiplier — shown in-game). The net ratio maps to at most ±20 loyalty/turn (full ±20 at a 3.0:1 pressure ratio).

Other per-turn identity sources (exact values):

- Garrisoned unit / martial law: 8
- City follows your founded religion: 3
- City follows a religion you didn't found: -3
- Starvation: -4
- Occupation (max): 10
- City-states (free cities pressure): 20
- Free cities: 10

Loyalty bands (yield/growth penalties by level):

- **Unrest** (0–25): yields -100%, growth +0%, identity change ×0.25
- **Disloyal** (26–50): yields -50%, growth +25%, identity change ×0.5
- **Wavering Loyalty** (51–75): yields -25%, growth +75%, identity change ×0.75
- **Loyal** (76–100): yields +0%, growth +100%, identity change ×0.0

City captured in war: loyalty set to 50. City flipped by loyalty or liberated: 100. Spy Foment Unrest: -15 loyalty (-5 more per spy level).

## Era score, Golden / Dark / Heroic Ages

Base thresholds each era: **Dark Age below 14 era score**, **Golden Age at 28+**; between them is a Normal Age. Each past Golden Age shifts your future thresholds 5 higher; each past Dark Age shifts them -5. Per-era threshold shifts also apply (Eras_XP2.EraScoreThresholdShift below). A Golden Age immediately after a Dark Age is a **Heroic Age** (choose 3 dedications). The live snapshot renders your actual thresholds — trust it over the base math.

Per-era data (game-era minimum/maximum turns, era-score threshold shift):

- **Ancient**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift -3; Great Person base cost 30; warmonger points 0
- **Classical**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 60; warmonger points 6
- **Medieval**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 120; warmonger points 12
- **Renaissance**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 240; warmonger points 18
- **Industrial**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 420; warmonger points 24
- **Modern**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 660; warmonger points 24
- **Atomic**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 960; warmonger points 24
- **Information**: era length 40–60 turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 1320; warmonger points 24
- **Future**: era length ?–? turns; threshold shift 0; Great Person base cost 1320; warmonger points 24

### Dedications (commemorations)

- **Free Inquiry**: normal age — Free Inquiry Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you trigger a Eureka. +1 Era Score for constructing a building that provides Science as a base yield. | golden age — Free Inquiry Golden Age: Eurekas provide an additional 10% of technology costs. Commercial Hub and Harbor district's Gold adjacency bonus provides Science as well. | dark age — Free Inquiry Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you trigger a Eureka. +1 Era Score for constructing a building that provides Science as a base yield.
- **Pen, Brush, and Voice**: normal age — Pen, Brush, and Voice Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you trigger an Inspiration. +1 Era Score for constructing a building with a Great Work Slot. | golden age — Pen, Brush, and Voice Golden Age: Inspirations provide an additional 10% of civic costs. Each city receives +1 Culture for each specialty district | dark age — Pen, Brush, and Voice Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you trigger an Inspiration. +1 Era Score for constructing a building with a Great Work Slot.
- **Monumentality**: normal age — Monumentality Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you construct a new specialty District. | golden age — Monumentality Golden Age: +2 Movement for all Builders. May purchase civilian units with Faith. Builders and Settlers are 30% cheaper to purchase with Faith and Gold. | dark age — Monumentality Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you construct a new specialty District.
- **Exodus of the Evangelists**: normal age — Exodus of the Evangelists Dedication Bonus: Gain +2 Era Score each time you convert a city to your founded Religion for the first time. | golden age — Exodus of the Evangelists Golden Age: +2 Movement for all Missionaries, Apostles, and Inquisitors. Additionally, newly trained ones get +2 Charges. +4 Great Prophet points per turn. | dark age — Exodus of the Evangelists Dedication Bonus: Gain +2 Era Score each time you convert a city to your founded Religion for the first time.

Gain +1 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian naval unit in combat. | golden age — Hic Sunt Dracones Golden Age: +3 starting Population for cities settled on a different continent than your first city. +2 Movement for naval and embarked units. +2 Loyalty per turn for cities not on your original Capital's continent. | dark age — Hic Sunt Dracones Dedication Bonus: Gain +3 Era Score each time you discover a new Continent or natural wonder. Gain +1 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian naval unit in combat.
- **Reform the Coinage**: normal age — Reform the Coinage Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you successfully complete a Trade Route. | golden age — Reform the Coinage Golden Age: Your Traders cannot be plundered. Campus district's Science adjacency bonus provides Production as well. | dark age — Heartbeat of Steam Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score for each Industrial or later building constructed.
- **To Arms!**: normal age — To Arms! Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian Corps in combat and +2 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian Army in combat. | golden age — To Arms! Golden Age: Unlock a special Casus Belli which generates 75% less Grievances than Formal War and can be used immediately after Denouncing the target. +15% Production towards military units. | dark age — To Arms! Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian Corps in combat and +2 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian Army in combat.

Gain +1 Era Score each time a Great Person is earned or purchased.

Receive 3 Uranium per turn. Uranium mines accumulate +1 more resource per turn. | dark age — Automaton Warfare Dedication Bonus: Gain +1 Era Score each time you kill a non-Barbarian unit with a Giant Death Robot.

## Alliances (R&F/GS)

3 levels per alliance. Alliance points accrue per turn (base 4× multiplier bucket: 1 for an active trade route, 2 for deals, 2 for shared government/religion factors). Level 2 at 320 points, level 3 at 960. An alliance lasts 30 turns. Allies share visibility and cannot declare war on each other. Types and level effects:

- **Research Alliance** — L1: add science to origin trade route | L1: add science to destination trade route | L2: research agreement | L3: science sharing from ally
- **Cultural Alliance** — L1: no culture pressure | L1: add culture to origin trade route | L1: add culture to destination trade route | L2: adjust district great people points | L3: tourism sharing from ally | L3: culture sharing from ally
- **Economic Alliance** — L1: add gold to origin trade route | L1: add gold to destination trade route | L2: envoy points from alliance | L3: share suzerain
- **Military Alliance** — L1: adjust combat strength | L2: share visibility | L2: increase production when war | L3: free unit upgrade
- **Religious Alliance** — L1: no religious pressure | L1: add faith to origin trade route | L1: add faith to destination trade route | L2: adjust religious combat strength | L3: yields from following ally religion | L3: religious pressure

## Emergencies (15 defined)

- **Military Emergency**: trigger take city; duration 30 turns; open borders among members: True; shared visibility: True
- **City-State Emergency**: trigger none; duration 5 turns; open borders among members: True; shared visibility: True
- **City-State Emergency**: trigger capture city state; duration 30 turns; open borders among members: True; shared visibility: True
- **Religious Emergency**: trigger convert city; duration 30 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **Nuclear Emergency**: trigger nuke used; duration 60 turns; open borders among members: True; shared visibility: True
- **Betrayal Emergency**: trigger war declared; duration 60 turns; open borders among members: True; shared visibility: True
- **Nobel Prize in Literature**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **Nobel Peace Prize**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **Nobel Prize in Physics**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **Aid Request**: trigger player loses pop to random event; duration 30 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **Military Aid Request**: trigger war with grievances; duration 30 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **World's Fair**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **International Space Station**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **Climate Accords**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False
- **World Games**: trigger world congress; duration 29 turns; open borders among members: False; shared visibility: False

Emergency gold reward scale: 400 gold per member per era (base). Joining an emergency via favor costs 30 favor.

## Diplomatic favor (GS)

Per-turn favor sources (exact values):

- Being suzerain of a city-state: +1/turn each
- Each active alliance: +1/turn
- Government base favor: see Governments (Vol 5) — tier-dependent per-turn favor
- Holding another civ's original capital: -5/turn per capital
- Grievances against you reduce favor income: −1 per 50 grievances (floor -10/turn)
- High CO2 contribution reduces favor: −1 per 3 lifetime CO2 (floor -20/turn)
- One-time: liberate a city-state +100, liberate a civ's city +100, revive a dead civ +200

### World Congress resolutions

- **Diplomatic Victory** (from Modern) [special session only]: A — Chosen Player gains 2 Diplomatic Victory points. | B — Chosen Player loses 2 Diplomatic Victory points.
- **Luxury Policy**: A — Duplicates of the chosen Luxury resource grant Amenities. | B — The chosen Luxury resource grants no Amenities.
- **Trade Policy**: A — Trade Routes sent to the chosen player provide +4 Gold to the sender. The chosen player receives +1 Trade Route capacity. | B — Cancels any international Trade Routes between other civilizations and the chosen player, and embargoes any new ones from starting.
- **World Religion**: A — +10 Strength (Combat and Religious) for all units of this Religion. | B — All players may condemn units of the chosen Religion, and doing so grants 25 Diplomatic Favor.
- **Mercenary Companies**: A — Producing, or purchasing military units using the chosen currency type, is +100% of the cost until the next World Congress. | B — Producing, or purchasing military units using the chosen currency type, is -50% of the cost until the next World Congress.
- **Arms Control** (from Atomic): A — All players have their Weapons of Mass Destruction set equal to the target player's. | B — The target player loses all of their Weapons of Mass Destruction.
- **Heritage Organization** (from Modern): A — Tourism from Great Works of this type is doubled. | B — No Tourism from Great Works of this type.
- **World Ideology** (from Modern): A — This Government type gains a Wildcard policy slot. | B — This Government type loses a Wildcard policy slot.
- **Urban Development Treaty**: A — +100% Production towards buildings in this district. | B — No buildings can be created in this district.
- **Border Control Treaty**: A — New districts built by this player act as Culture bombs. | B — This player's borders will not grow via Culture.
- **Public Works Program** (from Atomic): A — +100% Production towards this Project. | B — -50% Production towards this Project.
- **Patronage**: A — Earn double points towards Great People of this class. | B — No points earned towards Great People of this class.
- **Global Energy Treaty** (from Modern): A — Ban the production of buildings of this type. | B — 50% discount on the production of buildings of this type.
- **Sovereignty**: A — +100% of the City-States' yield type when sending Trade Routes to a City-State of this type. | B — City-States of this type do not provide their unique Suzerain bonus.
- **Migration Treaty** (from Industrial): A — +20% faster Population growth but -5 Loyalty per turn in this player's cities. | B — +5 Loyalty per turn but -20% Population growth in this player's cities.
- **Deforestation Treaty** (from Atomic): A — Prohibits chopping or clearing Features of the chosen type. | B — Clearing Features of the chosen type yields Gold equal to the Production and Food.
- **Public Relations**: A — The chosen player generates 100% more Grievances, and other players generate 100% more Grievances toward this player. | B — The chosen player generates 50% fewer Grievances, and other players generate 50% fewer Grievances toward this player.
- **Espionage Pact** (from Industrial): A — Spies executing the chosen Operation function 2 levels higher. | B — The chosen Operation is unavailable.
- **Military Advisory**: A — Units of the chosen promotion class gain +5 Combat Strength. | B — Units of the chosen promotion class lose 5 Combat Strength.

## Grievances (GS replaces warmonger points)

Key values: denouncement 25; declaring war on a city-state with envoys 50 (suzerain: 100); conquering a city-state gives all players 50; holding a conquered capital 3/turn, non-capital 1/turn; broken promises multiply grievances ×2. Grievance decay per era: Ancient 10/turn, Classical 9/turn, Medieval 8/turn, Renaissance 7/turn, Industrial 6/turn, Modern 5/turn, Atomic 4/turn, Information 3/turn, Future 2/turn.

## Climate & disasters (GS)

CO2 per 1°C of warming scales by map size: Duel 500000, Tiny 1000000, Small 1500000, Standard 2000000, Large 2500000, Huge 3000000. 50% of unit resource consumption counts toward CO2. 45% of coastal lowland tiles flood over the full climate-change track. Random events and their per-degree scaling:

- **1000 Year Flood** (severity 2): The river bursts its banks, and rising water covers the land for miles around. Not for a thousand years has the river flooded to such an extent! Chance +20% per degree of warming; mitigated damage reduction 50%.
- **Catastrophic Eruption** (severity 1): Kilimanjaro roars, and a plume of smoke and ash jets into the sky, as people and animals flee in terror! Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Catastrophic Eruption** (severity 1): People living near the volcano flee as lava and ash blankets the surrounding land. Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Catastrophic Eruption** (severity 1): People must go far out of their way to avoid the huge plume of ash that erupts from Eyjafjallajökull. Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Category-4 Hurricane** (severity 1): Pelting rain and a howling gale mark the arrival of a mighty hurricane. Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Category-5 Hurricane** (severity 2): The wind screams, the torrents of rain fall, and the waves drive inexorably ashore. Little can stand where this hurricane passes! Chance +50% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase I** (severity 1): 0.5 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase II** (severity 2): 1.0 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase III** (severity 3): 1.5 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase IV** (severity 4): 2.0 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase V** (severity 5): 2.5 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase VI** (severity 6): 3.0 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Climate Change Phase VII** (severity 7): 3.5 Chance +0% per degree of warming.
- **Crippling Blizzard** (severity 2): The howling wind and lashing snow turn sky and land white. Familiar forms disappear beneath frozen mounds. Chance +50% per degree of warming.
- **Forest Fire** (severity 1): The trees catch alight, creating an unstoppable fire that will rage across the landscape. Only you could have prevented this. Chance +50% per degree of warming.

## Power (GS)

Buildings that require power operate at reduced effect when unpowered (production penalty for unpowered industrial buildings caps at -50%). Power requirements and generation per building are listed inline in Vol 3 ("requires N power" / "generates N power"). Power plant fuel consumption uses the plant's listed resource; renewable sources (Hydroelectric Dam, Wind Farm, Solar Farm, Geothermal Plant) generate clean power. Late civics/techs add clean-power projects.

## Strategic resource stockpiles (GS)

Strategic resources accumulate per turn from improved copies and are SPENT to build units (see per-unit costs in Vol 6) and consumed per turn as fuel by some late units and power plants. Stockpile caps grow with era and buildings (Encampment buildings +10 each for land-unit resources, Harbor buildings for naval). Extraction rate: improved strategic tiles yield per-turn accumulation (boosted by relevant buildings/policies). Exact live numbers (current stockpile, cap, accumulation) come from the tracker snapshot (Phase D2).

## Faith units for tourism (GS)

- **Naturalist**: faith cost 800 (cost rises per purchase); A late-game civilian who can create a single National Park to attract Tourists. Must be purchased with Faith.
- **Rock Band**: faith cost 300 (cost rises per purchase); Can perform a rock concert at a valid venue, including at Wonders, at a District with one of the required buildings, or at a special target allowed by one of the band's promotions. Their Album Sales stat is the expected Tourism strength at their next concert. After performing concerts their Album Sales and Rock Band Level may increase. Must be purchased with Faith. Cannot perform on the same tile twice.
